subject.title: [Feature] Telegram Inline Query Support (@botname in any chat)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in Telegram inline-query support inside the bundled Telegram plugin, and what authorization, cache, session, and execution defaults should it use?
rationale: The implementation path is clear, but routing arbitrary-chat inline query text into agents changes a Telegram security boundary and needs maintainer-owned product/security defaults before automation can safely implement it.

options.title: Approve constrained opt-in inline mode
options.body: Add `channels.telegram.inlineQueries` or an equivalent explicit opt-in with account-level authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for user-specific results, bounded agent execution, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer behind Guest/Bot-to-Bot design
options.body: Keep this open until the broader arbitrary-chat Telegram ingress design settles and then implement inline queries using the shared approved boundary.

options.title: Reject core inline mode for now
options.body: Decline built-in inline-query support and document that operators should use separate Telegram bots until OpenClaw has a safer extension seam.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained opt-in inline mode
recommendation.body: Add `channels.telegram.inlineQueries` or an equivalent explicit opt-in with account-level authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for user-specific results, bounded agent execution, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Telegram handler/config provenance and recent adjacent Telegram work make this the best available owner for the security/product boundary decision.
